newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK LEAPS, HITS RECORD IN BUDAPEST, LONDON.
newsitem.headline: TVK LEAPS, HITS RECORD IN BUDAPEST, LONDON.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals company Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat Rt were surging to new record levels in early trading in Budapest and London on Wednesday, still benefiting from market talks of an imminent payout by the state to the company, traders said.
TVK is expected to cash in five billion forints and an additional one billion of accumulated interest under the provisions of Hungary's previous privatisation law.
"Six billion forint is a pretty substantial amount compared to their overall result," one London trader said.
TVK rallied to new records of 3,255 forints in Budapest and of $17.75 in London's SEAQ, before retreating a little in both markets.
In London, TVK was marked at $17.3 at 1000 GMT and in Budapest it traded at 3,185 forints at 1008 GMT, up 190.

"I doubt that market talks of the five billion forints is the only reason behind the rally, although it contributed," one Budapest-trader said, but added that he was not aware of any other factors. "Foreigners show demand for huge amount of TVK shares."
Until 1010 GMT 1.24 million TVK shares changed hands on the Budapest market, representing 5.16 percent of the chemicals firm's 24 billion forints issued share capital.

Another trader in Budapest mentioned market talks behind TVK's surge, saying that own shares that TVK last year bought from the local governments will be revalued in the company's books and this will have a positive impact on TVK's earnings.
TVK was not available for immediate comment.
